title: Insulin Pump Program Revenue-Cycle Standard: Payer Claims and Remittance Postings
content:
**RC-1 Original claims.** Every refill shipped on a payer tier of the Insulin Pump Program is billed to the payer named by the program's coverage record by one original claim per shipment, with the ship date as the date of service; the self-pay tier files no claims.

**RC-2 Timely filing.** An original claim must be transmitted no later than the tier's timely-filing limit in calendar days after the date of service of the shipment it bills, counted in calendar days from that ship date with the last day allowed. A shipment whose filing limit has passed is billed to neither the payer nor the customer and is written off by Larkfield.

| Hypothetical case (90-day limit, ship date D) | Original claim |
|---|---|
| Transmitted on day D plus 90 | Within the limit |
| Transmitted on day D plus 91 | Too late — written off by Larkfield, never billed to the customer |

**RC-3 Corrected and void claims.** A corrected claim replaces an original claim when the units, item or dates billed were wrong or some of the units were returned, and a void claim withdraws an original claim when all of its units were returned; both reference the same shipment as the original.

**RC-4 Patient responsibility on a remittance.** When a remittance posts, the patient responsibility added to the customer's balance is the allowed amount less the amount the payer paid, which the remittance itemizes as deductible, coinsurance and copay. *This clause is no longer in force for a remittance posting under review for a billing correction, whose supportable patient responsibility follows its current review rule; every other remittance posting of the program remains under it.* Larkfield never posts more than that and never bills the customer the difference between its billed charge and the allowed amount on a payer tier.

*Hypothetical example:* a remittance allowing $120.00 on which the payer paid $96.00 leaves $24.00 of patient responsibility; a billed charge of $150.00 does not raise that figure.

**RC-5 Secondary coverage.** On tiers where crossover to a secondary coverage applies and the customer has an in-effect secondary coverage record, the patient responsibility is crossed over to the secondary payer, and the secondary payer's payment is posted as a balance adjustment for a secondary payer payment against that remittance before any amount is statemented; on other tiers a secondary coverage is billed by Larkfield's billing team only after the primary remittance posts.

**RC-6 Medicaid.** On the Medicaid tier a customer is never billed for a Medicaid-covered item beyond the patient responsibility the Medicaid remittance shows.
